description: A disk whose mount unit would have a name past 255 bytes, which systemd names by a hash Atoll does not compute, is left out of the rule, as the daemon mounts it again itself: the command exits with 4, the rule printed all the same. With no unit to name, every failed disk or none at all, the rule lets atoll start no mount unit, and the command exits with 0 when no disk in service is left out.
config:
pool_id = "home-media"
catalog = "${SANDBOX}/catalog.db"
[view]
mount = "${SANDBOX}/pool"
[[disk]]
id = "t1"
uuid = "3f1c9a2e-5b7d-4c1e-9a0b-2d4f6e8a1c3b"
mount = "/mnt/disk1"
fs = "ext4"
state = "failed"
[[disk]]
id = "t2"
uuid = "7a2b4c6d-8e0f-4a1b-9c2d-3e4f5a6b7c8d"
mount = ""
fs = "ext4"
